note.question: What determines a stylized supply chain model consisting of n buyers and two suppliers?
note.overview: Yield uncertainty is a ubiquitous and serious issue in supply chain management. A common mitigation strategy for buyers is dual sourcing: ordering the same good from multiple suppliers to hedge against uncertainty in the suppliers’ ability to fulfill orders. In the literature, it is typically assumed that there is a single buyer that knows or can learn the reliability of each supplier, which is assumed to be exogenous to the buyer’s ordering behavior.

source.quote: However, in this model (and in contrast to most of the dual-sourcing literature), the buyers do not know the suppliers’ inventory distribu­ tions or fulfillment likelihood.

Although we model UV as full disclosure of I, Section 7 discusses how coarser public signals and trusted intermediaries could be used to implement UV without requiring buyers to have full knowledge of I.

Our model is motivated by industries in which (i) short-run supply is subject to yield or quality shocks, (ii) capacity is highly sticky in the short run, (iii) a large set of downstream buyers competes for output from a small number of upstream suppliers, and (iv) buyers primarily observe their own fill-rate outcomes rather than the state of upstream supply.
